gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sony says phones, TVs and PCs cannot receive the PS-LX3BT's Bluetooth stream, or that Bluetooth-only use requires setting the rear OUTPUT SELECT switch to LINE.
standout_why: I compared against platterandplinth.com/turntables/best-with-preamp, valveandvinyl.com/turntables/crosley-alternatives, stylusandsound.com/best-turntables-with-built-in-preamp and blog.burtonacoustix.com/turn-table/best-turntable-for-beginners. Platter & Plinth already gives the PS-LX3BT's codecs (SBC, aptX, aptX Adaptive), its fixed headshell and Sony's statement that no other styluses are supported. Stylus & Sound and Valve & Vinyl already cover the VM95-series stylus path for the AT-LP70X. Burton Acoustix already gives the AT-LP70XBT's codecs (aptX Adaptive, aptX, SBC) and its wired-plus-Bluetooth behaviour. None of them states Sony's exclusion of phones, TVs and PCs as receivers. None states that the OUTPUT SELECT switch must be on LINE for Bluetooth-only use. None points out that neither Bluetooth deck lists AAC. Stylus & Sound says the Sony 'streams to Bluetooth speakers, headphones or soundbars' and stops there. Valve & Vinyl only says the PS-LX310BT does not receive Bluetooth, which is the other direction. fewbetter.com has no turntable content at all. vinylpickup.com would not load (certificate error), so I could not check it.
decides: This confirms the AT-LP70X or Fluance RT81 as the pick for anyone who wants to stream records to a phone, TV or PC, because the Sony Bluetooth deck sends only to speakers or headphones. For a shopper who wants Bluetooth and uses AirPods or other Apple earbuds, the PS-LX3BT gains nothing from aptX Adaptive. Its codecs are SBC, aptX and aptX Adaptive, with no AAC, so those earbuds get SBC. That makes the cheaper AT-LP70XBT ($299 in ChatGPT's card) at least as good a choice as the $349.99 Sony. A shopper with an aptX Adaptive speaker or headphones is the exception: only then does the Sony's 96 kHz/24-bit 'Hi-Res Wireless' mode apply.

findings.label: Devices that cannot receive its Bluetooth stream
findings.value: TVs, smartphones and PCs cannot receive the turntable's Bluetooth stream
findings.note: Translated from Sony's Japanese text: 'テレビやスマートフォン、パソコンなどの機器は、本機とBluetooth接続して本機から送信されるストリーミングを受信することはできません'. This is Sony Japan's page for the same global model number. Sony's US and Canadian pages returned 403, so I have no US-page wording.

findings.label: Switch setting required for Bluetooth-only use
findings.value: Set the rear OUTPUT SELECT switch to LINE
findings.note: Sony's text: 'Bluetooth接続だけで使用する場合は、本体背面のOUTPUT SELECTスイッチをLINE側に切り替えてご使用ください'. The same page also warns against connecting headphones that have no volume control, because playback may be very loud.

findings.label: Requirement for Hi-Res Wireless
findings.value: Needs an aptX Adaptive receiver for 96 kHz/24-bit
findings.note: Sony's text: 'Hi-Res WirelessはaptX Adaptiveに対応した再生機器をお使いください'.

findings.label: Bluetooth transmit codecs
findings.value: SBC, aptX, aptX Adaptive (no AAC listed)
findings.source_title: PS-LX3BT 主な仕様 | Sony Japan
findings.note: Sony's spec line: '対応コーデック（送信）：SBC, aptX, aptX Adaptive'. My inference, not Sony's statement: AirPods and other AAC/SBC-only headphones would connect over SBC.

findings.label: Headshell, speeds, outputs
findings.value: Headshell not replaceable (moulded plastic); 33⅓ and 45 rpm; phono output 2.5 mV and line output 180 mV at 1 kHz; gain Low −4 dB / Mid 0 dB / High +6 dB; MM cartridge at 3.5 ± 0.5 g tracking force
findings.source_title: PS-LX3BT 主な仕様 | Sony Japan
findings.note: Spec table rows: 交換ヘッドシェル 非対応, 33 1/3回転・45回転. There is no 78 rpm.

findings.label: USB recording compatibility
findings.value: USB Type-B (USB 2.0) records WAV at 44.1/48 kHz, 16-bit; works with Windows 11 and macOS 13–15 using built-in drivers; USB cable sold separately; recording software must be installed
findings.source_title: PS-LX3BT 主な仕様 | Sony Japan
findings.note: MP3, DSF and DSDIFF recording are marked 非対応 (not supported). The requirement for a separately sold cable and recording software comes from feature_2 on the same site.

unsourced: AT-LP70X / AT-LP70XBT codecs, cartridge (AT-VM95C) and replacement stylus (AT-VMN95 series): every audio-technica.com regional page (en-us, en-gb, /turntables/all/) returned 403. I found no AT manual PDF, so I'm leaving out AT figures that rest only on retailers.

Fluance RT81 / RT81+ cartridge and stylus pairing (AT95E ↔ ATN95E on the RT81, AT-VM95E ↔ AT-VMN95 on the RT81+): fluance.com product URLs returned 404, storecheck returned HTTP 404 and I found no Fluance manual. Only retailers and third-party sites state the pairing.
Whether the PS-LX3BT's wired output and Bluetooth can play at the same time: Sony's Japanese pages don't say, Sony's US and Canadian spec pages returned 403, and I found no Sony Help Guide page.
US prices for all candidates: Sony US (electronics.sony.com) and Audio-Technica US blocked the fetch, Fluance's store URL returned 404, and I did not run amzcheck within the call budget.
